$comment: Document package schema (spec §1.1). `include` decides whether the document is generated at all; `groupOrder` fixes article order within it. Every clause must declare a group that appears in its document's groupOrder — validate.mjs enforces this so a clause can never be silently dropped during numbering. Each document declares the `package` it belongs to, so the UI can distinguish a document excluded within the chosen package from one that belongs to a different package entirely, and `label` gives it a stable name for library views where the templated title has nothing to interpolate.

documents.rationale: Always required — this is the filing that creates the entity.
documents.label: Charter filing

documents.rationale: Always required — governs how the owners run the Company.
documents.label: Governing document

documents.rationale: Included when the industry is IP-critical or there is more than one founder — either way, ownership of the work has to sit with the Company rather than with an individual.
documents.label: Founder IP Assignment

documents.rationale: Included for institutional funding or multiple founders — vesting is what protects the team from an early departure taking dead equity with them.
documents.label: Founder Vesting Agreement

documents.rationale: Included for C-Corp stock subject to vesting. The filing deadline is 30 days and cannot be extended.
documents.label: IRS Section 83(b) Election

documents.rationale: Always required — the first corporate act, which adopts everything else in the package.
documents.label: Initial Consent

documents.rationale: Included when hiring within 12 months. Wage-and-hour exposure starts at the first hire.
documents.label: Employment Policy Set

documents.rationale: Included when the operating state differs from the formation state.
documents.label: Foreign Qualification

documents.rationale: Always generated — obligation extraction across the whole package (spec §4.2).
documents.label: Compliance Calendar

documents.rationale: Always generated — the governing document and IP assignment both refer to attachments, and a reference to an attachment that does not exist is a defect the consistency checker reports.
documents.label: Schedules and Exhibits

documents.rationale: Always first in a commercial engagement — it is the document that lets the parties talk about scope at all.
documents.label: Mutual NDA

documents.rationale: The framework agreement. Everything commercial and legal lives here so each statement of work can stay short.
documents.label: Master Services Agreement

documents.rationale: Scope, deliverables, and price. Kept separate from the MSA so a second engagement does not reopen the legal terms.
documents.label: Statement of Work

documents.rationale: Attached when personal data is in scope. For most buyers this is a precondition to signature, not a nice-to-have.
documents.label: Data Processing Addendum

documents.rationale: Generated for an employee hire. Carries at-will language, classification, and the policies the handbook expands on.
documents.label: Employment Agreement

documents.rationale: Generated for a contractor engagement. Deliberately omits the supervision and benefits language that would undercut the classification.
documents.label: Independent Contractor Agreement

documents.rationale: The policies that have to exist before the first employee starts, not after.
documents.label: Employee Handbook
